explanation: The exposure lasted several minutes, so traffic and walkers left no trace. A man having his boots polished stood still long enough to appear, probably the first person ever photographed.

claims.text: Louis Daguerre's 1838 photograph of the Boulevard du Temple shows almost no people because its long exposure did not record moving people and traffic.
The boulevard looks empty in Daguerre's photograph not because it was closed, painted out or cleared by rain.
The exposure for Daguerre's Boulevard du Temple photograph lasted several minutes.
A man having his boots polished appears in the photograph and is often described as probably the first person ever photographed.
